parts.title: [PART 1] My building has 12 floors, but the elevator keeps stopping at 13
parts.description: I thought our old elevator was malfunctioning until I saw what was waiting on the thirteenth floor. Then my elderly neighbor recognized something I couldn't see, and the building manager started acting strangely.
parts.story_so_far: A tenant discovers that their elevator sometimes opens onto a mysterious thirteenth floor. After witnessing increasingly disturbing events, they discover their neighbor knows something about the building's secret, while the manager appears determined to conceal it.

post.title: My building only has 12 floors, but the elevator keeps stopping at 13. My neighbor knows why.

lines.text: My apartment building has twelve floors, but last night the elevator opened onto a hallway that shouldn't exist.
I know it sounds ridiculous, but I've lived here for eight months, and I've seen the number 13 appear on that display three separate times.
There's no thirteenth-floor button. I've checked. The elevator goes from the basement straight through twelve.
The first time, the doors opened onto a hallway that looked almost identical to mine. Except the lights were dead, the carpet was soaking wet, and every apartment number had been scratched off.
Then I heard a child laughing somewhere in the darkness. I held the close button until the doors finally shut.
I reported it to the building manager. He immediately asked if I'd been drinking, then told me old wiring sometimes caused strange displays.
But here's what bothered me. When I asked whether he'd ever seen thirteen himself, he stopped smiling and told me to forget about it.
So I started keeping a written log of every incident, including the exact time and floor. I also recorded the elevator display on my phone.
Three weeks later, it happened again. This time, the doors opened just a few inches. Through the gap, I saw a woman standing with her back toward me.
She wore a long, dark coat. Her hair was completely wet, and one hand was pressed against the hallway wall.
I pressed the close button. The woman slowly turned her head without moving her body. I couldn't see her face, but I knew she was looking directly at me.
That night, someone stood outside my apartment for almost an hour. I heard the footsteps stop directly in front of my door. I didn't look through the peephole.
The third time, I wasn't alone. I was riding with an elderly neighbor named Mrs. Vale, who lived in apartment 8B.
The elevator stopped. Thirteen appeared on the display. Before the doors even moved, Mrs. Vale dropped her shopping trolley.
She grabbed my arm and whispered, 'Don't let it open.'
I held the close button. Something began dragging its fingernails across the other side of the elevator doors.
Mrs. Vale started shaking. Then she looked at me and said something I'll never forget.
'It knows you live here now.'
Before I could ask what she meant, the lights went out. A voice came from somewhere inside the elevator.
'Which one is yours?'
The lights returned. We were back on eight. Mrs. Vale ran out without her trolley and locked herself inside 8B.
The following morning, I found her trolley outside my apartment. A note was attached to the handle. It said, 'I'm sorry. It asked me first.'
I photographed the note and immediately contacted the police. But when they arrived, it had disappeared. So had Mrs. Vale.
Her furniture was untouched. Her bed was made. Even her purse was sitting on the kitchen table with her keys inside.
The manager claimed she'd gone to stay with relatives. I demanded their contact information. He refused, then ordered me to stop investigating.
That's when I decided I wasn't going to trust another word he said. I kept copies of my recordings and my incident log somewhere he couldn't access them.
I took the stairs for six months. I avoided the elevator completely. Then one rainy evening, I came home carrying a box of old photographs my sister had mailed me.
The stairwell lights were dead. I heard the elevator moving above me. It passed the eighth floor, then the ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth.
Then it stopped. I looked through the stairwell window. The display was glowing.
Thirteen.
The doors opened, and I could see that same wet hallway. But this time, someone was standing at the far end.
It was Mrs. Vale. Same green cardigan. Same shopping trolley. She raised one finger to her lips, then pointed directly behind me.
I turned around. There was a door in the concrete stairwell wall. I'd walked past that exact spot hundreds of times.
It had a brass number plate. Eight C. My apartment was 8A. Mrs. Vale's was 8B.
And the handle was slowly turning from the other side.

parts.title: [PART 2] The photograph inside my apartment was dated 14 years before I was born
parts.description: A mysterious door marked 8C appears in my stairwell, and the photographs inside my delivery box reveal something impossible. But the building manager has been hiding a much bigger secret than a faulty elevator.
parts.story_so_far: After six months of avoiding the elevator, the narrator discovers a mysterious apartment marked 8C beside their own. An old photograph reveals that the narrator, Mrs. Vale, and the building manager were apparently together fourteen years before the narrator was born.

post.title: UPDATE | I found an apartment marked 8C that wasn't on the building plans. Then I saw an old photograph.

lines.text: I was standing in my apartment building's dark stairwell, staring at a door marked 8C, when I heard my own voice coming from behind it.
The handle turned again. I dropped the box of photographs and stepped backward. Pictures scattered across the concrete floor.
I looked through the photographs, hoping to find something that would explain what was happening. Most were old family pictures.
Then one landed face up. It showed the lobby of my building, with the elevator behind a group of people smiling at the camera.
I recognized Mrs. Vale. She was standing beside the building manager. But there was another person between them.
It was me. Same face. Same scar above my eyebrow. Even the little birthmark on my neck was there.
I turned the photograph over. The date was written in faded ink. Fourteen years before I was born.
I immediately took pictures of the photograph and sent them to my sister. Then I remembered the manager's behavior and decided to check something.
Before moving in, I'd received a copy of the building's original floor plan. It showed twelve floors, but there was no apartment 8C anywhere.
I pulled out my phone and called the manager. He answered after two rings.
I asked him one question. 'Who lived in apartment 8C?'
There was silence. Then he said, 'Where did you see that number?'
I told him I was in the stairwell. He immediately told me to leave the building and wait outside.
I asked why. His response made my stomach drop.
'Because that apartment belongs to someone who hasn't moved out yet.'
I looked at the door. The lock clicked. It opened another inch.
A smell came through the gap. Dust, rain, and something sweet that had started to rot.
Then I heard a child laughing inside. The exact same laughter I'd heard on the thirteenth floor.
And then my own voice spoke from inside the room.
'Which one is yours?'
I ran. I didn't even stop to collect the photographs. I made it outside and called the police again.
This time, I gave them the recordings, the incident log, and the photograph. I also told them about Mrs. Vale and the manager's refusal to provide any information.
They sent officers to the building. The manager was waiting in the lobby. He looked furious when he saw me.
He insisted that I was confused and that apartment 8C didn't exist. One officer asked him to produce the original building records.
The manager refused. Then another officer noticed something behind the reception desk. An old brass key with a tag that read 8C.
The manager tried to take it, but the officer stopped him. He finally admitted that he'd known about the strange floor for years.
He claimed previous tenants had reported the same thing. Some disappeared from their apartments, while others left behind photographs of people who hadn't been born yet.
When I asked why he'd never warned anyone, he said the building had been operating normally for years and he didn't want to cause panic.
I told him that was a convenient excuse for someone who kept hiding missing tenants and denying documented incidents.
The officers took the key and secured the building records. The manager was removed from his position while the investigation continued.
I moved out three days later. I never found Mrs. Vale, and nobody could explain the photograph.
My sister eventually sent me another envelope containing the remaining photographs from the same collection. I'd almost forgotten about them.
There was one photograph I hadn't seen before. It showed the same lobby, the same elevator, and the same group of people.
But this time, the picture was taken from inside the elevator. Everyone was looking toward the camera.
Everyone except me. I was standing at the back, facing the open doors. Behind me was a dark hallway with wet carpet.
I turned the picture over. There was a handwritten message underneath.
'Eight C. Reserved for the next tenant.'
I threw the photograph into the trash. But that night, at exactly 2:13 AM, my new apartment's elevator stopped outside my floor.
I checked the security camera feed. The hallway was empty. The elevator display showed thirteen.
Then my phone rang. It was an unknown number. I answered, and a familiar elderly woman's voice whispered:
'You shouldn't have left your photographs behind.'
I looked toward my front door. Something was sliding a photograph underneath it.
I picked it up. It was a picture of my new apartment building.
And somewhere in the background, barely visible through the lobby windows, was an elevator with a thirteenth-floor button.
